title: Nonzero torus-stable central vector subgroup of a split unipotent group
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Groups are affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after every field extension. Write $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ and $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A represented fppf quotient means a group scheme representing the sheafification of the right-coset functor for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras. A smooth geometrically connected group is split unipotent if it admits a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation with unipotent geometric points and a finite descending series of smooth geometrically connected subgroups, each normal in its predecessor, with represented fppf successive quotients isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a$. An action by group automorphisms is a $k$-morphism satisfying the action identities and preserving multiplication after every commutative $k$-algebra extension. Let $U\ne1$ be split unipotent and let $E=\mathbf G_m^s$, $s\geq0$, act on $U$ by group automorphisms. There exist an integer $d\geq1$, a smooth geometrically connected subgroup $C\subseteq U$ stable under $E$, and a $k$-group isomorphism $C\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$. Moreover $C$ is central in $U$: for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, $u\in U(R)$ and $c\in C(R)$ one has $ucu^{-1}=c$. The chosen isomorphism need not make the $E$-action linear. No perfectness, infinitude or characteristic assumption on $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Conrad--Lichtenstein, Linear Algebraic Groups I, Appendix D.3, proof of Theorem D.3.2, printed p.86: central vector subgroup in positive characteristic and normality under the ambient split solvable group. In characteristic zero use the smooth central subgroup of a unipotent group and its vector-group structure (Milne, Corollary 14.55 and Proposition 14.32). Read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/252Page/handouts/alggroups.pdf. WANTED locally: the Conrad notes, Appendix D.3; the arbitrary-field central split subgroup prerequisite is not Milne Corollary 16.23, which assumes perfectness.

proof.text: First suppose $\operatorname{char}k=0$. Let $Z=Z(U)$, the represented closed commutative centre, and let $C=Z^0$ with its open-and-closed subgroup structure. Cartier smoothness makes $C$ smooth, and the identity section makes the connected $C$ geometrically connected. Since $k$ is perfect, the central-additive-subgroup lemma gives a closed $N\simeq\mathbf G_a$ in $Z$. Its connected image contains the identity, hence lies in the open-and-closed component $C$. Thus $C\ne1$.

source.place: Characteristic-zero branch: Milne Proposition 14.32, printed p.289, central subgroup and vector-group argument; centre and identity component spelled out by Q82.

proof.text: The geometric-unipotence lemma embeds $U$ as a closed subgroup of some upper unitriangular $\mathcal U_n$. Restriction gives a closed embedding of $C$ into $\mathcal U_n$: on affine coordinate algebras it is the composite of two surjections. Hence the characteristic-zero commutative-vector-group lemma applies to $C$, giving $C\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$. Since $C\ne1$, $d\ne0$, so $d\geq1$. This supplies the required central subgroup in characteristic zero, with invariance checked below.

source.place: Milne Proposition 14.32 and Corollary 14.33, printed p.289, applied to the connected centre.

proof.text: Now suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. In a split additive series for the nontrivial $U$, the last nontrivial term is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a$, since its next term is $1$. Its inclusion gives a nonconstant morphism $\mathbb A^1_k\to U$. Thus $U$ is not $k$-wound. Let $F$ be its canonical central smooth connected subgroup killed by $p$. The cckp-kernel criterion implies that $F$ is not $k$-wound.

source.place: Conrad--Lichtenstein, Linear Algebraic Groups I, Appendix D.3, proof of Theorem D.3.2, printed p.86, positive-characteristic central vector subgroup; refined using Conrad, The structure of solvable groups over general fields, Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2, pp.15--16 (online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; WANTED locally).

proof.text: Apply the vector--wound decomposition to the smooth connected commutative $p$-torsion group $F$. Write $F=C\times W$ with $C\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$ the canonical vector factor. Because $F$ is not wound, the criterion $C=1\Longleftrightarrow F\text{ is wound}$ gives $d\geq1$. The factor is a closed smooth geometrically connected subgroup of $U$ and central there, since $C\subseteq F$. Geometric connectedness follows directly from $C\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$: polynomial rings over fields are domains. No perfection assumption was used.

source.place: Conrad, The structure of solvable groups over general fields, Theorem 2.6 and Corollary 2.7, pp.12--13, refining the vector-subgroup paragraph in Conrad--Lichtenstein Appendix D.3, p.86; online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; WANTED locally.

proof.text: Put $K=k_s$. In characteristic zero, $Z(U)_K=Z(U_K)$; the open-and-closed connected subgroup $C_K$ is its identity component, since $C$ is geometrically connected. Every $K$-group automorphism of $U_K$ therefore preserves $C_K$. In characteristic $p$, $F_K$ is the cckp-kernel of $U_K$, so every $K$-group automorphism of $U_K$ preserves $F_K$ by its largest-subgroup characterization. It also preserves $C_K$: composing with that automorphism permutes all pointed affine-line morphisms into $F_K$, whose smallest containing closed subgroup is $C_K$. Consequently in either characteristic each $e\in E(K)$ preserves $C_K$.

source.place: Conrad--Lichtenstein Appendix D.3, p.86, passage to the separable closure and automorphism stability; Conrad Definition 3.1 and Theorem 2.6 give the precise canonical subgroups. Characteristic-zero component argument supplied by Q82.

proof.text: It remains to pass from these automorphisms to the action morphism. Let $I$ be the ideal of $C$ in $k[U]$. Pull back $f\in I$ along $E\times C\to U$, obtaining a Laurent polynomial $P_f\in k[C][t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_s^{\pm1}]$. After extension to $K$, evaluation at every $e\in(K^\times)^s$ is zero by the previous step, as an element of $K[C_K]$. Choose a basis of the finite-dimensional $K$-span of its coefficients. Each resulting scalar Laurent polynomial vanishes on $(K^\times)^s$ and is zero: multiply by a monomial and apply the univariate root bound successively in each variable over the infinite field $K$. Thus all coefficients vanish. Injectivity of $k[C]\to k[C]\otimes_kK$ gives $P_f=0$. Therefore the restricted action factors through $C$; its action identities are inherited from those on $U$. For $s=0$ there are no variables and evaluation is already the identity. Centrality gives $ucu^{-1}=c$ on every algebra, as required.

source.place: Agent-written affine-coordinate verification of the smooth-action invariance argument in Conrad--Lichtenstein Appendix D.3, p.86; no assertion about pointwise density over the original field is used.

proof_origin.place: Characteristic-zero branch: Proposition 14.32, p.289. Positive-characteristic branch follows the canonical-subgroup argument of Conrad--Lichtenstein Appendix D.3, p.86, made precise by Conrad (2014), Definition 3.1/Proposition 3.2 and Theorem 2.6/Corollary 2.7. Both Conrad documents read online but WANTED locally. Assembly and Laurent coefficient argument by Q82.

lean.statement: theorem exists_splitUnipotent_central_vector_subgroup {k : Type u} [Field k] (U : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hU : SolvableGroupStructure.IsAlgebraic U) (hunipotent : SolvableGroupStructure.IsUnipotent U) (hsplit : ∃ n : ℕ, SplitUnipotentLength U n) (hne : ¬ Nonempty (U ≅ Grp.trivial _)) (s : ℕ) [a : ModObj (MultiplicativeType.splitTorus k s).X U.X] (hautomorphism : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (e : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k R ⟶ (MultiplicativeType.splitTorus k s).X) (x y : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k R ⟶ U.X), lift e (x * y) ≫ a.smul = (lift e x ≫ a.smul) * (lift e y ≫ a.smul)) : ∃ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d ∧ ∃ (C : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (i : C ⟶ U), IsClosedSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ Smooth C.X.hom ∧ GeometricallyConnected C.X.hom ∧ Nonempty (C ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin d ↦ Grp.mk (StandardGroupSchemes.additive k))) ∧ (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (e : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k R ⟶ (MultiplicativeType.splitTorus k s).X) (c : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k R ⟶ C.X), ∃ c' : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k R ⟶ C.X, c' ≫ i.hom.hom = lift e (c ≫ i.hom.hom) ≫ a.smul) ∧ (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (x : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k R ⟶ U.X) (c : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k R ⟶ C.X), x * (c ≫ i.hom.hom) * x⁻¹ = c ≫ i.hom.hom)
